provisions.title: Standard of consent
provisions.text: (1) The consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, and shall signify an agreement to the processing of her personal data for the specified purpose and be limited to such personal data as is necessary for such specified purpose.

provisions.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies
provisions.text: The product's intended functionality exposes information to certain actors in accordance with the developer's security policy, but this information is regarded as sensitive according to the intended security policies of other stakeholders.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: In routes/saveLoginIp.ts the route loads the full User record with UserModel.findByPk(loggedInUser.data.id) and then returns the updated object with res.json(updatedUser). No attributes allow-list, toJSON override or field-level scrubbing appears in the Evidence. The User model in models/user.ts has sensitive properties: the password field, whose setter stores security.hash(clearTextPassword), plus other redacted secret-type fields and internal fields like role, lastLoginIp and profileImage. Because the whole model instance is serialised, every column, including the password hash and any secret or token fields, goes into the HTTP response. That is the whole-model serialisation pattern of the positive example, and it is not narrowed with attributes the way the negative example is. The record belongs to the logged-in user, not another user's object, so object-level authorization (API1) is not the issue. The issue is excessive property exposure (API3) and missing safeguards on stored credential data.
